newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada Q4 housing starts rise 0.4 pct.
newsitem.headline: Canada Q4 housing starts rise 0.4 pct.

text.p: Canadian housing starts rose by 0.4 percent in the fourth quarter of 1996 to a seasonally adjusted annual rate (SAAR) of 129,300 units from a revised 128,800 units in the third quarter, the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corp (CMHC) said on Friday.
Actual housing starts fell to 32,446 in the fourth quarter from 37,190 the quarter before. The SAAR is a monthly figure adjusted to remove normal seasonal variation and multiplied by 12.

The housing corporation said housing construction in the fourth quarter maintained the pace from the previous three months and was expected to remain steady in the near term.

"Recent increases in mortgate rates are unlikely to dampen housing starts activity significantly. In fact, improving economic conditions will push new home construction higher in the months ahead," said Michel Laurence, senior economist with the CMHC's market analysis center.
